stem: A 12-year-old boy with acute lymphoblastic leukemia has a leukocyte count of 180,000/mm3 with predominantly lymphoblasts. Induction chemotherapy begins tomorrow. To protect his kidneys from the expected release of intracellular contents, he is started on aggressive hydration and an oral drug that lowers uric acid formation.
oneliner: 12M + ALL, WBC 180,000 + chemo tomorrow + hydration and an oral drug that lowers urate formation → works how?
ask: The oral drug protects his kidneys by which of the following mechanisms?

options.A: Conversion of uric acid to allantoin

whyNot.A: **Rasburicase**: IV recombinant enzyme, not an oral drug
whyNot.B: **Probenecid** raises urinary urate and could **worsen** nephropathy
whyNot.C: A **chemotherapy** mechanism, not a uric acid drug

why: **Huge blast count before chemotherapy** = risk of **tumor lysis syndrome**. **Allopurinol** inhibits **xanthine oxidase**, so purine breakdown stops at hypoxanthine and xanthine and **less uric acid** reaches the kidney.

drug.name: Allopurinol
drug.how: Blocks conversion of hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid
drug.use: Chronic gout, tumor lysis prophylaxis, uric acid stones
drug.watch: Rash (severe with HLA-B*58:01), raises azathioprine and 6-MP levels (needs dose cut), hepatotoxicity

stem: A 58-year-old man has had five attacks of gouty arthritis in 18 months despite colchicine prophylaxis. His creatinine is normal and he has no history of kidney stones. Serum uric acid is 10.6 mg/dL and a 24-hour urine collection contains 350 mg of uric acid. His physician chooses a drug that increases urinary uric acid excretion.
oneliner: 58M + five gout attacks in 18 mo on colchicine + serum urate 10.6 + 24-h urine urate 350 mg (low) → drug that raises excretion works how?
ask: The drug acts by which of the following mechanisms?

options.C: Blocking urate reabsorption in the proximal tubule

whyNot.A: **Colchicine**: he is already on it, and it does not lower urate
whyNot.B: **Ketorolac / NSAIDs**: treat the acute attack, not the urate level
whyNot.E: **Rasburicase / pegloticase**: IV enzymes, not an excretion drug

answer: URAT1 blockade in the proximal tubule (probenecid)
why: **Low urinary urate with high serum urate** = **underexcretor**. **Probenecid** blocks **URAT1** in the proximal tubule, so **less urate is reabsorbed**.

drug.name: Probenecid
drug.how: Inhibits URAT1 (organic anion transporter) in the proximal tubule, blocking urate reabsorption
drug.use: Chronic gout in underexcretors; prolongs penicillin levels
drug.watch: Uric acid stones (keep urine alkaline and hydrated), raises penicillin and methotrexate levels, avoid aspirin; useless in overproducers

stem: A 64-year-old man with squamous cell carcinoma of the lung has 1 week of confusion, polyuria, constipation and thirst. Serum calcium is 14.2 mg/dL, phosphate is low and PTH is suppressed. After 2 L of intravenous saline his calcium is 13.6 mg/dL. An intravenous drug is added that lowers calcium over the next 2 to 4 days.
oneliner: 64M + squamous cell lung cancer + confusion, polyuria, constipation + Ca 14.2, PTH suppressed + still 13.6 after saline + IV drug added → works how?
ask: The added drug lowers his calcium mainly by which of the following mechanisms?

options.D: Increasing calcium excretion in the thick ascending limb

whyNot.B: PTH is **already suppressed**; the tumor releases PTHrP
whyNot.D: **Furosemide**: acts within hours, only after volume repletion; not a bone-directed drug
whyNot.E: Helps in **vitamin D excess**; this takes days and is not the target here

why: **Squamous lung cancer + high calcium + low PTH** = hypercalcemia of malignancy (PTHrP). After saline, an IV **bisphosphonate** (pamidronate or zoledronic acid) **inhibits osteoclasts** and lowers calcium over days.

drug.name: Zoledronic acid / pamidronate
drug.how: Pyrophosphate analog that binds hydroxyapatite and inhibits osteoclast resorption
drug.use: Hypercalcemia of malignancy, bone metastases, Paget disease, osteoporosis
drug.watch: Fever and bone pain after first dose, hypocalcemia, renal toxicity, osteonecrosis of the jaw, atypical femur fracture

chain: Osteoclasts take it up and are inhibited

stem: A 66-year-old postmenopausal woman has an L1 compression fracture after lifting a grocery bag. DXA shows a T-score of -3.0 at the hip. She is started on weekly alendronate.
oneliner: 66F + postmenopausal + L1 compression fracture + hip T-score -3.0 + alendronate started → works how?
ask: The drug increases bone density mainly by which of the following mechanisms?

whyNot.A: That is **teriparatide**, given daily by injection
whyNot.C: Would **raise** osteoclast activity and bone loss
whyNot.D: Osteoprotegerin is a **decoy for RANKL**; lowering it increases resorption
whyNot.E: Raises calcium absorption but has **no effect** on osteoclast resorption

why: **Fragility fracture + low T-score** = osteoporosis. **Bisphosphonates** bind **hydroxyapatite**, are taken up by osteoclasts and **reduce bone resorption**.

drug.name: Alendronate
drug.how: Pyrophosphate analog that binds bone and inhibits osteoclast function
drug.watch: Pill esophagitis, osteonecrosis of the jaw, atypical femur fracture, hypocalcemia

stem: A 58-year-old man has a hot, red, swollen great toe since last night. Joint fluid shows needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals under polarized light. He cannot take NSAIDs because of a bleeding ulcer, and is given a drug that stops the flare but does not change his serum urate.
oneliner: 58M + acute red great toe + needle crystals, negatively birefringent + NSAIDs contraindicated + drug stops the flare but leaves urate unchanged → mechanism?
ask: Which is the mechanism of the drug given?

options.A: Inhibits xanthine oxidase, reducing production of uric acid
options.B: Blocks URAT1 in the proximal tubule to increase urate excretion
options.C: Recombinant uricase converting urate into allantoin
options.E: Inhibits cyclooxygenase to lower prostaglandin synthesis

whyNot.A: That is **allopurinol or febuxostat**; they lower urate and are not used for acute flares
whyNot.B: That is **probenecid**; it lowers urate and is not started during a flare
whyNot.C: That is **pegloticase**, for refractory gout, and it lowers urate
whyNot.E: That is an **NSAID**, which he cannot take because of the ulcer

answer: Binds tubulin and blocks microtubule polymerization
why: **Colchicine binds tubulin** and prevents microtubule polymerization, so **neutrophils cannot migrate or degranulate** in response to urate crystals. It treats and prevents flares without lowering serum urate. Diarrhea is the commonest adverse effect.

drug.name: Colchicine
drug.how: Binds tubulin and blocks microtubule polymerization, impairing neutrophil chemotaxis and degranulation
drug.use: Acute gout flare, gout prophylaxis, pericarditis, familial Mediterranean fever
drug.watch: Diarrhea and cramps first; bone marrow suppression and myopathy in overdose or with renal impairment

idea.rule: Colchicine quiets the neutrophils; it does not touch the urate.
also: Acute flare: NSAIDs, colchicine or glucocorticoids
Adverse effects: diarrhea, then bone marrow suppression
Also used in pericarditis and familial Mediterranean fever
